anya: Quick heads-up from the v6-small PTQ onboarding smoke: overall NDCG@10 unchanged but short-query MRR@5 slipped ~4.3%. No tokenizer differences.

dmitri: ok. same pattern we've seen but let's try a slightly different angle: measure score binning / entropy instead of only ties.

anya: I added a small probe to the harness to compute score bins (quantized buckets) and a "score_bin_entropy" per-query metric. Pseudocode: ```python
# simple binning probe
bins = np.round(scores / eps) * eps
entropy = -sum(p * log p for p in np.unique(bins, return_counts=True)[1] / len(bins))
```

carmen: nice. also run a seed sweep: 5 different RNG seeds for the candidate sampler and stable-sort (lexsort) vs numpy.argsort to check stability.

kevin: PTQ compresses dynamic range -> fewer unique bins -> lower entropy -> more fragile top positions. If entropy drops at p95 for top-3, that's a smoking gun.

anya: kicked off 6 runs (seeds 100..105), each with FP32 and PTQ. For each we record: top-3 MRR, NDCG@10, top-3 score_bin_entropy p50/p95, and rank_stability_p95 (fraction of queries where top-1 differs FP32 vs PTQ). CI job: https://ci.redwood/job/1899

ci-bot: job-1899 started by anya
logs: https://ci.redwood/job/1899/logs

anya: short summary:
- NDCG@10: FP32 vs PTQ ~within noise (+0.001)
- MRR@5 (short queries) mean drop: 4.2% across seeds
- score_bin_entropy (top-3) p50: FP32 1.85, PTQ 1.12
- score_bin_entropy (top-3) p95: FP32 2.10, PTQ 1.05
- rank_stability_p95 (top-1 change rate): ~3.9% of queries differed
So PTQ compresses bins and reduces entropy at the top, correlating with MRR loss.

dmitri: that correlation is solid. Let's prioritize mitigations that don't require full revert: (A) add lexsort stable tiebreaker by (score desc, original_pos asc) in eval and prod ranking, (B) add "last-layer fp16" flag for quant schemes and validate effect, (C) add rankbench smoke that runs seeded PTQ sweep and asserts rank_stability_p95 < 1% and MRR drop < 1%.

carmen: slight nuance: lexsort on floats is fine but make sure we use kind='stable' or np.lexsort with integer secondary key, avoid relying on platform-specific np.argsort. Document in harness.

anya: quick experiment results:
- stable lexsort only: MRR gap -> 1.1%
- last-layer fp16 only: MRR gap -> 0.7%
- lexsort + last-layer fp16: MRR gap -> 0.2%
Both metrics and seed sweep included in artifacts.

kevin: perfect. Add persistent metrics to telemetry: score_bin_entropy_top3, rank_stability_top1, topk_exact_tie_frac. We can surface trends per-model+quant-config.

sam: I'll add the rankbench job: seeded-sweep (5 seeds) + assert hooks and upload histograms. Also add a short unit test that forces two equal scores and checks deterministic tie-break fallback.

ci-bot: job-1899: artifacts uploaded -> https://ci.redwood/job/1899/artifacts (histograms + seed-manifest + configs)

tess: thanks team. please open PR with: (1) lexsort tie-breaker shim in eval + prod ranker, (2) rankbench seeded smoke, (3) telemetry metric definitions and dashboard entries, (4) small docs note on when to enable last-layer fp16 fallback. Tag me and eng-oncall.

anya: will open PR and INF issue. Creating INF-9991: "quant bin entropy regression: add lexsort tiebreaker, last-layer-fp16 flag, rankbench sweep" assigned to anya.

carmen: nice work catching this with a different signal (entropy). Much better than blind revert.

anya: PR will include the small probe code and a brief writeup correlating score_bin_entropy and MRR. Linking when ready. :rocket:
